[[File:X-Files CCG original logo.png|thumb|right|180px|Original X-Files CCG logo.]]
The '''X-Files Collectible Card Game''' is based on the television series ''The X-Files''. The United States Playing Card Company published it in 1996. Ron Kent and Duncan Macdonell are credited as designers.<ref name="x-files-original-rules">[https://www.cardgamecollector.com/images/x-files-ccg/X-Files-Basic-Rulebook.pdf The X-Files Collectible Card Game: Official Rules and Procedures Manual], The United States Playing Card Company, 1996. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20221125180805/https://www.cardgamecollector.com/images/x-files-ccg/X-Files-Basic-Rulebook.pdf Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="x-files-products">[https://www.cardgamecollector.com/x-files-ccg/index.html The X-Files Collectible Card Game], Card Game Collector, original set and game credits. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260415003400/https://www.cardgamecollector.com/x-files-ccg/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

Players investigate sites and collect clues to identify the opponent's hidden X-File.<ref name="x-files-original-rules" /> The ''101361'' expansion appeared in 1997.<ref name="x-files-expansion">[https://www.tcdb.com/Checklist.cfm/sid/268054/1997-USPlayingCardTheXFilesCCGVer.2101361Expansion 1997 US Playing Card The X Files CCG Ver. 2 101361 Expansion], Trading Card Database, product checklist. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261107204230/https://swccg.com/snapshots/tcdb/x-files-ccg-101361.html Internet Archive].</ref>

== Playing online ==

[[TCGMix]] offers an [https://tcgmix.com/xfiles/ X-Files browser playtest] with a tutorial, rooms and bot opponents.<ref name="x-files-online">[https://tcgmix.com/xfiles/ X-Files CCG on TCGMix]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261107193655/https://tcgmix.com/xfiles/ Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="catalog" />
